contradiction.viewer_thinks: the microwave cooks food from the inside out
contradiction.actually: the field dies within a few centimetres: the outer shell absorbs first and heat conducts inward

beats.narration: The box reheats your dinner in minutes — yet the plate scalds while the middle stays cold. Whatever is happening in there, it is not reaching the centre.
beats.claim: in microwave reheating the food's centre can stay cold while the outer parts and the container become hot
beats.visual_question: why does the middle of the food stay cold?
beats.visual_answer: a glowing wave front wraps the outside of a food block while its core sits dark and unheated

beats.narration: The picture most of us carry: waves beaming straight through the food, cooking it from the inside out.
beats.claim: the popular picture holds that microwaves cook food from the inside out
beats.visual_question: what do people picture inside the oven cavity?
beats.visual_answer: rays drawn straight through the food block, with a bright core marked inside-out

beats.narration: Follow the field and the story flips. Microwaves penetrate only a few centimetres into wet food. The outer shell takes the energy; the middle is warmed by plain conduction, like any oven.
beats.claim: microwaves penetrate only a few centimetres into wet food, so the outer shell absorbs the energy directly and heat reaches the centre by conduction
beats.visual_question: how deep does the microwave energy actually reach?
beats.visual_answer: the glowing field fades out over the first centimetres of the food block; the core is reached by a slow conduction gradient

beats.narration: The heating itself is dielectric. A field swinging two and a half billion times a second torques every water molecule, one after another — and jostling neighbours scrape that swing into heat.
beats.claim: a microwave oven heats food dielectrically: an oscillating electric field torques polar water molecules and molecular collisions dissipate the energy as heat
beats.visual_question: what does the oscillating field do to water molecules?
beats.visual_answer: water dipoles flip back and forth with the swinging field; friction between neighbours radiates heat

beats.narration: That is why frozen food sulks. Ice locks its molecules into a lattice — frozen water barely answers the field, so a defrost cycle trickles power in slowly.
beats.claim: ice absorbs microwave energy far more weakly than liquid water because its molecules are bound in a lattice, which is why defrost cycles use low power
beats.visual_question: why does frozen food heat so slowly?
beats.visual_answer: rigid lattice rows hold the dipoles locked while the liquid side flips freely and heats

beats.narration: And the scalding plate? The field pattern shifts with every load — part standing wave, part food shape — piling energy at the edges. The turntable is not a gadget; it is the apology the oven makes for that pattern.
beats.claim: the oven's field pattern changes with the food load and tends to concentrate energy near edges, so turntables and stirrers average out the hot spots
beats.visual_question: why do the edges burn while the centre waits?
beats.visual_answer: a patchwork hot-spot map concentrates energy at the food's rim; the turntable swings the load through it

beats.narration: So the plate scalded while the middle stayed cold for one reason: the field only heats the outer shell, and conduction carries the rest inward. Stir and rest the food — the cold centre is physics, not a broken oven.
beats.claim: microwave heating works at the food's outer shell and conduction plus stirring redistribute the heat; standing and resting food evens the temperature
beats.visual_question: so what is the right way to reheat?
beats.visual_answer: the food block with an even warm gradient after stirring, the field glow calm across the whole shell

visual_contradiction.seems: waves cook food from the inside out
visual_contradiction.actually: the field fades within a few centimetres — the outer shell absorbs first and conduction carries heat inward
visual_contradiction.reveal: the glowing field visibly dies across the first centimetres of the food block, leaving the core to a slow conduction gradient

payoff_image.image: the food block at rest with one even warm gradient through the shell and a calm field glow — the whole mechanism settled in a single frame
